Call Out Case - Blazar
Blazar : New entrant in Indian hair color & care market. A Brazilian company with global revenues of USD 500 mn, growing at 25% 5yr CAGR, same 
markets’ share of growth 55%, same market share of base 65%, GM 70%, Ebitda 30%. Operates in 6 countries around the globe [Brazil, USA, UK, Italy, 
Nigeria, Japan] while exporting to 40 more countries.
Blazar , founded by a second generation entrepreneur from a family of small retailers, started operating in Brazil out of a garage 20 years back focussing on 
niche & premium natural hair care using authentic ingredients. Over time, the business started finding far more success in hair colors, which were ubiquitous 
in Latin America [65% of revenue]. It’s a USD 2.7 bn industry there. Blazar has a 5% overall share but a 20% share in the premium end of the market. The 
model used by Blazar was largely in-salon sales through a professional & a retail line. Blazar hair colors have sold through a range of fashion colors 
proposition supported by natural additives as a secondary lever. Of late, the business has also started experimenting with a few proofs of concept in opening 
hair salons – however, that has not done well. Blazar continues to experiment with the same. Blazar is backed by a very strong R&D. 
Blazar now wants to enter Indian market. The Indian hair care market is roughly $3.3 bn growing at 10%. The hair color market is around 20% of that growing 
at 20% yoy. Almost 15% of hair care and 30% of hair colors are used professionally. Further, around 15% of hair care and 5% of hair color is sold for home use 
through salons. Average EBITDA in the category ranges from 12% to 23% with cheaper formats having a higher margin. 
Hair care in the market includes shampoos, rinse off conditioners, pre conditioners, leave in conditioners, styling gels, mousse and waxes with product 
segmentation operating on scalp type and cleansing / moisturizing / volumizing benefits. Hair colors include 3 major formats – powder [popularly called dyes] 
selling at Rs. 10 per use, hair cremes operating at Rs. 50 – 500 per use, henna operating at Rs. 100 for 5 uses. They constitute 30%, 50% and 20% of the 
market growing respectively at 5%, 20%, 30%. In terms of shades, India is a black & dark brown dominated market [60% growing at 4%] with burgundy next 
at 30% growing at 25% and rest of the vibrant shades at 10% growing at 20%. 
Blazar wants to enter the hair color & / or care market. Backed by a private equity fund now, it has resources to consider a stronger 
entry. What‘s the brand → business strategy over 10 years that you’d recommend?

Call Out Case - Blazar
Blazar : New entrant in Indian hair color & care market. A Brazilian company with global revenues of USD 500 mn, growing at 25% 5yr CAGR, same markets’ 
share of growth 55%, same market share of base 65%, GM 70%, Ebitda 30%. Operates in 6 countries around the globe [Brazil, USA, UK, Italy, Nigeria, Japan] 
while exporting to 40 more countries.
Blazar, founded by a second generation entrepreneur from a family of small retailers, started operating in Brazil out of a garage 20 years back focussing on niche & 
premium natural hair care using authentic ingredients. Over time, the business started finding far more success in hair colors, which were ubiquitous in Latin 
America [65% of revenue]. It’s a USD 2.7 bn industry there. Blazar has a 5% overall share but a 20% share in the premium end of the market. The model used by 
Blazar was largely in-salon sales through a professional & a retail line. Blazar hair colors have sold through a range of fashion colors proposition supported by 
natural additives as a secondary lever. Of late, the business has also started experimenting with a few proofs of concept in opening hair salons – however , that has 
not done well. Blazar continues to experiment with the same. Blazar is backed by a very strong R&D. 
Blazar now wants to enter Indian market. The Indian hair care market is roughly $3.3 bn growing at 10%. The hair color market is around 20% of that growing at 
20% yoy. Almost 15% of hair care and 30% of hair colors are used professionally. Further , around 15% of hair care and 5% of hair color is sold for home use through 
salons. Average EBITDA in the category ranges from 12% to 23% with cheaper formats having a higher margin. 
Hair care in the market includes shampoos, rinse off conditioners, pre conditioners, leave in conditioners, styling gels, mousse and waxes with product 
segmentation operating on scalp type and cleansing / moisturizing / volumizing benefits. Hair colors include 3 major formats – powder [popularly called dyes] 
selling at Rs. 10 per use, hair cremes operating at Rs. 50 – 500 per use, henna operating at Rs. 100 for 5 uses. They constitute 30%, 50% and 20% of the market 
growing respectively at 5%, 20%, 30%. In terms of shades, India is a black & dark brown dominated market [60% growing at 4%] with burgundy next at 30% 
growing at 25% and rest of the vibrant shades at 10% growing at 20%. 
Blazar wants to enter the hair color & / or care market. Backed by a private equity fund now, it has resources to consider a stronger entry. What‘s the brand → 
business strategy over 10 years that you’d recommend?

• Believability of a proposition launched by brand in question against competitors on the above drivers
• Extent of scrutiny undertaken on a proposition launched by brand in question against competitors on the above drivers

BrandFaithSM XtentSM measurement & application …
BrandFaithSM XtentSM can be measured through research based on the following proprietary model:
1. Determine the importance of drivers of customer choice in the category in the following buckets for different customer segments:
Delivery | Features | Aesthetics | Usage experience | Service | Advocacy | Price
2. Research the response of each segment on the following key metrics:
• Current associations of different brand with above drivers
• Default expectations from  a new entrant in the category on the above drivers
• Default expectations on innovations launched by different brands in the market on the above drivers
• Believability of a proposition launched by brand in question against competitors on the above drivers
• Extent of scrutiny undertaken on a proposition launched by brand in question against competitors on the above drivers
3. This would give the BrandFaithSM XtentSM for the brand in question for each driver cited
4. BrandFaithSM XtentSM for each driver multiplied by the importance of each driver for the category in general & brand in particular 
would give composite BrandFaithSM XtentSM for the category as well as for the brand in question. 
5. This would in turn not just give the extent of EVA [PAT less cost of capital deployed] attributable to the brand but would also give a 
sense of Branded Profit Pool for the category as a superset. From BrandFaith SM
